The registry, one claim per address

Registered claims and their falsifiers

21 claims. Each one carries its declared falsifier, the consequence fixed in advance, the repairs declared unavailable, and the date after which its warrant is stale. None of that is a summary of the claim — it is the claim's own record, rendered.

02How to read a date here

The expiry date is not a prediction that a claim will go wrong. It is the end of the review window recorded in the registry. A claim past its window is due, not false — and this site's CI fails the build rather than let a lapsed window pass quietly.

The same registry renders three ways: as one ledger, as decay clocks, and here as one page per claim. One source, three bandwidths.

03Machine-readable

Every claim page carries a schema.org Claim node whose falsifier, consequence, forbidden rescues and non-claims travel in the same object, under a published vocabulary. An agent that quotes a claim from this site has already been handed the condition under which the claim is withdrawn.

The whole registry as one JSON document: /claims/index.json.
